title: The numeral wall
summary: The four published readings stand as four big numbers across the page, and the numbers themselves are the buttons. Press one and the panel beneath explains it in plain words, shows it as a share of 100 on a single measured bar and names its source.
story: After the reframe says most teams fix the wrong layer, this section brings in outside authority (what the market's own research says about where deals are won) and hands the letter its cue with the line 'Not one of them moves with more activity'.
motion: Standalone mockup: the head plays as usual (label, the two statement lines rising, the red rule, the lede). After the lede, at 0.7s, the four numbers rise 12px out of their masks from left to right, 120ms apart, without counting. At 1.3s cell 01 takes its ink rule. The panel then writes itself in: the finding, the 'so what' and the detail, as 300ms fades from 1.45s. The red 17% bar extends from 1.85s to 2.55s (700ms), followed by its '17 / 100' flag, its unit line and the field-note link.

The automatic pass (round 6, now calm): 17 holds until 4.9s, about 3.5s after its finding appeared. Then the pass moves through 95:5 at 4.9s, 77 at 8.2s and 53 at 11.5s, and comes back to 17 at 14.8s. That is one reading every 3.3 seconds, where round 5 changed reading every 0.65 seconds. The red 17 bar lands again at 16.0s, everything has settled by 16.1s, and nothing moves after that. The pass runs once and never loops.

Each step of the pass: the old words fade out over 280ms while the bar draws back to zero with them. The new words then fade in over 420ms while the bar re-extends to the new value over 900ms, and the value flag fades in as the bar arrives. The new number's top rule draws in 600ms and its ink deepens in 420ms. Two readings are never on screen at once, and the bar never jumps.

Any interaction stops the pass at once, and it never restarts: a press (on a number, or anywhere in the readout), resting the pointer on a number (a real move onto it, then a fifth of a second), or keyboard focus (Tab into the row). The reading on screen stays. A step that is halfway through finishes where it was going.

Screen readers: the panel normally reads out the new reading after a press. While the automatic pass runs, nobody asked for it, so the panel stays quiet. It speaks again the moment the pass ends or anything stops it.

Each press: the panel crossfades in 360ms (the old reading fades out before the new one fades in, so two texts never overlap). The bar snaps to 0 and re-extends to the new value (600ms), and its value flag fades in as the bar arrives. Only 17 is red; the other three bars are ink. Presses keep this brisker tempo; only the automatic pass is slower.

Hover or keyboard focus on a number draws a grey rule across its top, darkens the number and its label to full ink, and outlines its small square in ink, inviting the press. A 1px focus frame marks keyboard focus.
Keyboard: the arrow keys move between the four numbers and select as they go. Home and End jump to the first and last. The whole row is one Tab stop.

On the live homepage the head plays as the section arrives. The numbers rise when their row is 40% on screen. The panel and the red bar wait until the panel itself is on screen, so the bar never fills below the fold, and never before cell 01's rule has landed. The same calm pass then follows: 17 holds 3.45s from its finding, then one reading every 3.3s, back to 17 and stop (settled 14.6s after the panel wrote in). It only moves on while the panel is on screen. If you scroll away it waits, and when you come back the reading on screen holds for a full 3.3s before it continues.
Reduced motion: the final state (17 selected, red bar drawn), with no timers and no automatic pass.
addressed: 'When it first loads to the section, the animation, when it plays, switches from one number to the other very quickly on its own. Maybe we could slow down the pace of switching': slowed about fivefold. Each reading now stays for 3.3 seconds, long enough to read its finding and its 'so what' (round 5 changed reading every 0.65 seconds). 17 gets a slightly longer first hold (about 3.5s from when its finding appears), so the section opens on its main point. The pass goes through once, 17 → 95:5 → 77 → 53, comes back to 17 and stops for good. It never loops.

The change itself is slower too, so the switch reads as a turn of the page rather than a flicker. The old words fade out as the bar draws back to zero, then the new words fade in as the bar extends to its new value (0.9s). The top rule on the new number draws in at the same pace. Nothing on the page moves or resizes while this happens: the panel keeps one fixed height, and this was measured at every frame of the pass.

It now also plays on the homepage, where you see it. It waits until the readout panel is on screen, holds 17, then steps at the same calm pace. If you scroll past before it finishes, it waits rather than playing out of sight, and picks up again when you come back.

It gets out of your way. As soon as you press a number, rest the pointer on one, or Tab into the row, the automatic pass stops and does not come back. The reading you are looking at stays put. Pressing a number keeps the brisk response you approved; only the automatic pass is slower.
notes: Stage 1100px at 1440. Head: standard .ac-head (statement cols 1–8, lede cols 1–6, no meta, no note). Wall: 80px below the lede. Four <button aria-pressed> cells on cols 1–3 / 4–6 / 7–9 / 10–12 sit inside role=toolbar (the ARIA pattern for toggle buttons with roving focus), with a roving tabindex. Each cell, top to bottom: an 8px selector square, its label, then the numeral. The numerals are .ac-num at 144px with units at .5em, light 300. 95:5 measures 231px in its 310px cell, so the 128px floor is not needed; at the 88px mobile size it fits its 164px cell. Readout: 48px below the wall. The four readings are stacked in one grid cell, so the panel is a fixed 160px whichever reading is shown, verified after every press. Text sits on cols 1–6 (claim 24px Mona 500, so-what 17px, detail 15px; every detail sets in 3 lines). MEASURE sits on cols 7–12: a 1px track with end ticks at 0 and 100 only, and a 10px bar. The value is flagged at the fill's end by a 1px pole. For 95:5, '95 not buying' is flagged at the far end. Then come the unit words (15px, one line) and 'Source · …' (.ac-cap). The field-note link (.ac-link) is the same for all four readings, so it sits apart on the panel's bottom line, level with the detail's last line. Copy: the claim, so, detail and source are verbatim from the live StructuralEvidence component, including its em dashes and its 'brand, product, and price'. Round 2's comma edits are dropped. Apostrophes are typographic. The U+2011 non-breaking hyphens are set as plain hyphens so the brand font renders them. Visible words at rest: 116 (cap 120). Red: the label square, the rule, and the 17% bar while 01 is pressed. Screen-reader-only text (not rendered): the toolbar label 'Four readings. Choose one to read it.' and '17 of 100.' (etc.) before each unit line. ≤760px: a 2×2 wall at 88px, then the readout stacked (text, then MEASURE), with 16px margins and the statement at 9.4vw. The door uses .1em tracking so it holds one line at 375px. Verified at 375px with no horizontal scroll. Review-round changes from STORY's literal build brief: (1) the readout splits 1–6 | 7–12 instead of 1–7 | 9–12. At 1–7 | 9–12 the bar started at x=955, under the % sign of 77% and on no edge of the wall, so it read as floating. Now both halves start on a cell edge (64 / 732), and the bar has 644px to work with instead of 422px. (2) The fixed height comes from stacking the readings (160px) rather than a 240px min-height, which only added dead space under the section. (3) The live trigger is split into two beats, the wall at 40% and the readout when it is itself visible, because the single wall trigger extended the red bar below the fold. · Promoted unchanged from round-2 slot S. · Round 6 (pace): the automatic pass now steps every 3.3s (was 0.65s) and runs on the homepage too. JS constants: HOLD 3300, FIRST 3450 (from the readout's claim), OUT 280 and EXT 900 (bar retract and re-extend per step), INTENT 200 (hover-intent). While it runs, the root carries .is-auto, which switches the crossfade and state tokens (--xo/--xi 280/420ms, --ct 420ms, --rt 600ms, --fo 240ms, and an in-out curve on the fade-out). Presses keep 160/200, 250, 360 and 120ms. During the pass the bar draws back with the old words and re-extends instead of snapping. A press snaps as approved. Halts: pointerdown (mouse or pen) or click (touch) anywhere in the explorer, focusin anywhere in it, and hover-intent on a numeral (a pointermove with real movement, then a 200ms rest). After a wheel scroll Chrome sends a hover update but no pointermove, so a still pointer that the page scrolls under does not halt the pass (tested). Homepage: an IntersectionObserver on the readout (ratio ≥ .34) gates each step. A step that falls due off screen waits, and when the readout returns the pass re-arms with a full hold. Verified by timed capture: standalone steps at 4.92 / 8.23 / 11.53 / 14.83s, settled by 16.04s. Panel opacities sampled every frame never show two readings above 2% at once. Section height, readout height and door position stay constant across the pass at 1440 and 375, in both skins, with zero layout-shift entries. demoMs 16000, so the final shot (≈16.6s+) is the resting 17% state. · Review pass (round 6): the readout's live region (aria-live=polite) is set to off from the moment the pass is armed, and back to polite when the pass ends or is halted. Halting happens on pointerdown or focusin, before the press changes the reading, so presses are still announced. The four automatic changes are no longer read out unprompted. Re-verified by timed capture: steps at 4.9 / 8.2 / 11.5 / 14.8s, no overlap, no layout shift; home pass, scroll-away pause, touch swipe and tap, keyboard and reduced motion unchanged.
deviations: Readout columns: 1–6 | 7–12 instead of STORY's 1–7 | 9–12, so the readout locks to the wall's cell edges; see notes.
Readout height: fixed at 160px by stacking the four readings, instead of the ~240px estimate; nothing reflows on a press.
Selector squares (8px, ink only, set before each label) are not in STORY's cell spec. They were added so the wall reads as a control in a still frame.
The value and '95 not buying' are set as drafting flags (a 1px pole up from the bar) rather than bare mono text. Their positions are unchanged.
The field-note link is the same for all four readings and sits on the panel's bottom line. Its date (June 2026) is not rendered, because STORY's door text omits it.
Live entrance is in two beats (wall at 40% visible, readout when on screen) rather than one '40% visible' trigger.
role=toolbar instead of a plain group, for the roving-focus toggle buttons.

Homepage start: the pass is anchored to the readout's entrance (it begins 3.45s after the readout writes in, which needs the readout on screen) rather than to the section reaching 40% in view. At 1440×900 the section is 40% in view while only its head is showing (the wall's top is about 130px below the fold), so a pass started there would step out of sight. The wall still rises at its own 40% trigger.

Off-screen pause (not in the brief): on the homepage the pass steps only while the readout is on screen. It waits while the readout is off screen and resumes with a full 3.3s hold, so it never plays out unseen.

Pass tempo differs from a press: the automatic pass uses a 280 + 420ms crossfade, a 600ms rule and a 900ms bar that draws back with the old words. A press keeps the approved 160 + 200ms crossfade, 360ms rule and 600ms snap-and-re-extend bar.

Halt triggers are a little wider than 'the row': a press or keyboard focus anywhere in the explorer halts the pass (for example selecting text in the readout, or tabbing to the field-note link), so the words never change under someone reading or copying them. Hover-intent is limited to the numerals.
An interrupted pass rests on the reading that was showing (or the one pressed), not on 17. Only an uninterrupted pass returns to 17.
